Berdyansk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaporizhia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Berdyansk (known as Osipenko from 1939 to 1958) had a Jewish presence from the city's founding in the early 19th century, growing from 162 people in 1857 to 3,048 (over 11 percent) by 1897; the city also had a Karaite community of 258 members, whose kenassa was closed by Soviet authorities in 1920. The community maintained two synagogues, a Talmud Torah, and separate schools for boys and girls, with both the Bund and Zionists active. Following the German occupation in October 1941, about 1,000 Jews were murdered within two weeks; in 1942, women in mixed marriages were murdered along with their children. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 19th century with its last burial in 1953, was demolished in two stages, per the Berdyansk Museum of Local Lore — most of it destroyed between 1947–1948 during construction of the Azovkabel plant, with the section holding the most elaborate tombstones surviving until further construction of a gas storage facility in 1987.
